thread.title: Cisco Vs. Juniper: Goliath Against David - Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) | Seeking Alpha

author: Hervé Blandin
title: Cisco Vs. Juniper: Goliath Against David - Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) | Seeking Alpha
text:
Up to two years ago, my job consisted of designing, implementing, and managing IT networks: I had been working with Cisco ( CSCO ) devices and services for fifteen years.
I could observe first hand the evolution of Cisco, from selling network boxes to expanding its empire into collaboration, security, wireless, and data centers. I have experienced the stickiness of Cisco solutions: switching costs and risks represent a high hurdle before considering replacing a Cisco network. Moreover, network engineers value Cisco over other vendors because of the large choice of well paid jobs around the world.
Witnessing this moat, I could not resist the low valuation in 2012 and became a shareholder. However, during these years, Juniper ( JNPR ) has been threatening Cisco's dominance. As I am always open to new ideas, I became interested in comparing both companies and their relative valuation. Does David stand a chance against Goliath?
Source of the picture
Same core business, different evolution Routing, switching, security, and wireless constitute the core businesses of both companies: they both sell network products and associated services like maintenance. The services revenues represent a similar proportion for both companies at 26% for Cisco and 30% for Juniper.
Cisco clearly dominates Juniper in terms of sales with almost ten times more revenues at about $48B against $5.03B for Juniper in 2017. Cisco employs nearly eight times more people (72,900) than Juniper (9,381).
While Juniper stays in its core competencies, Cisco has been expanding into collaboration and data centers, mainly through acquisitions. As a confirmation, Cisco recently announced it would focus on innovation and would shift to software and subscription based services. On its side, Juniper highlights its scalable, reliable, secure and cost-effective networks.
R&D amounts to 12.6% of Cisco revenues, at slightly more than $6B. Juniper spent almost $1B in R&D in 2017, representing 19.5% of revenues. Juniper must spend a higher percentage of revenues in R&D in order to keep up with much bigger competitors like Cisco. Even with a lower ratio of R&D expenditure, Cisco still spends $5B more than Juniper, which is equivalent to one year of Juniper's revenues! With this difference, Cisco should keep on building up its technological advantage over Juniper, or at least stay isolated from any durable technological edge from Juniper.
On the other hand, both companies allocate the same proportion of sales and marketing expenses: 19.1% for Cisco at $9.2B, against 18.9% for Juniper at $0.95B. It is interesting to note that Cisco, a well established and mature high tech company, spends much more money on marketing compared to R&D. The business model consists of, depending on the customers, offering large discounts based on expansive products price lists.
Cisco greatly profits from its scale thanks to important cross selling opportunities. For instance, with a strong network and wireless installed base, Cisco can sell collaboration, data centers, and security solutions benefiting from easier integration with the Cisco network and monitoring solutions already in place.
Moreover, Cisco's scale facilitates alliances with dominant actors. The partnership with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) leverages Cisco's existing solutions by implementing them in a vertical where Cisco is absent: the mobile phones. Apple has chosen Cisco in order to improve its presence in enterprises, taking advantage of Cisco's installed base.
Let's now check if the numbers support this business analysis.
Better operational performances for Cisco As expected and as shown on the table below, due to its bigger scale, Cisco benefits from better margins (I have ignored the exceptional charges due to the tax reform in 2017).
Cisco Juniper Gross margins Products 2017 61.6% 60.5% Gross margins Services 2017 66.8% 62.4% Gross margins average 2017 63% 61.1% Net margins last 5 years About 20% 12-13% ROE last 5 years About 15% About 10% Source: Author, based on annual reports
As a confirmation of the margins differences, revenues per employee amount to $658,436 for Cisco and $536,190 for Juniper.
With no surprise, profitability follows the same pattern as margins. The ROE at about 15% for Cisco is quite impressive considering that the company does not use leverage.
For Juniper, ROE varies much more over the years, depending on the exceptional items. Ignoring an $850M goodwill impairment for Juniper in 2014, ROE stays at an average of about 10%.
Cleaner balance sheet for Cisco In line with operational results, Cisco's balance sheet looks much better than Juniper's. The table below presents key differences from both companies latest quarterly reports.
Cisco Juniper Net cash $34B $1.66B Goodwill (% of assets) 27.8% 34% Deferred revenues (% of liabilities) 40.6% 26.4% Source: Author, based on latest quarterly reports
Although Juniper's balance sheet does not show any particular weakness (except for the slightly elevated goodwill), Cisco's balance sheet looks more attractive with proportionally more cash, more deferred revenue, and less goodwill.
We can also compare the evolution of the book values per share over the last five years, as shown on the table below.
Cisco Juniper BV/share beginning 2013 $10.36 $13.03 Dividends/share paid 2013-2018 $4.13 $1.76 BV/share 2018 $9.63 $11.99 Progression BV/share 2013-2018 32.8% 5.53%* Source: Author, based on latest quarterly and annual reports
* In 2014, Juniper recorded an $850M goodwill impairment due to the underperformance of its security unit. Without this exceptional item, the progression of the book value would have been 23.6%.
With a cleaner balance sheet, Cisco has been growing its book value per share faster than Juniper, demonstrating again its superiority.
Valuation comparison Relative to Juniper, Cisco clearly overperforms by all metrics: gross margins, net margins, better balance sheet, ROE,... Let's now compare their respective valuation in order to see if the market takes these differences into account.
The table below compares both companies with some valuation metrics.
Cisco Juniper EV/Sales (NYSE: TTM ) 3.46 1.61 EV/EBITDA ( TTM ) 10.64 7.61 EV/EBIT ( TTM ) 13.5 11.1 PER (last 5 years) 17.8 15.9 Price/book 3.97 2.2 Source: Author, based on latest quarterly reports and annual reports
For the PER, I have subtracted the net cash and I have considered the average net income over the last 5 years, ignoring the $850M goodwill impairment for Juniper.
The market clearly takes into account the superiority of Cisco. An opportunity could exist if the valuation gap between both companies changes. A narrower gap would make Cisco more attractive than today, relative to Juniper. Obviously, the other way around applies too.
Investors willing to invest in a network vendor can choose to pay a price in relation with the quality of the company. Over time, though, the relative valuations vary, as shown on the graph below.
Source: Boursorama.com
I consider that Cisco's moat and dominance will increase; therefore, I would buy Juniper only at an absolute low valuation and at a big discount to Cisco. I would reinforce my Cisco position should the market offer any dips in the stock price.
Conclusion Cisco and Juniper, with both established core businesses in the network area, are taking different paths. Taking advantage of its size, Cisco has been expanding into complementary businesses, while Juniper has been focusing on its core network competencies.
Cisco has been reinforcing its dominant position thanks to its scale, translating this superiority into impressive financial statements compared to Juniper. On the business side, Goliath wins.
Considering these results and its growing moat, the market correctly values Cisco at a premium compared to Juniper. On the valuation side and depending on the market mood, David still could win, though.
Disclosure: I am/we are long CSCO.
